does: Rolls a warm, soft food up in a bamboo mat and presses it, so that it sets into a firm, even block with square edges.

intro.what: A bamboo mat shapes warm soft food into an even block as it firms.
intro.why: It teaches you to use distributed pressure and warmth to control shape without cracking.

how: Lay the mat on the board with the bamboo sticks running side to side.
Place the warm food at the near edge and roll the mat over it tightly.
Press and squeeze along the whole length so that the sides are straight.
Leave it rolled in the mat for a short while to set, then unroll and cut.

cues.text: The block has an even shape with square edges.
The block is firm and holds together when it is cut.

mistakes.mistake: Rolling when the food is cold and stiff, so that it cracks.
mistakes.fix: Shape it while it is still warm.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing unevenly, so that one end is thinner.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the whole length of the mat with both hands.

quiz.question: What does pressing in the mat create?
choices: Loose pieces separated by the bamboo.
An even block with straight sides.
A thin sheet stretched across the board.
quiz.because: The rolled mat supports the food while pressure defines its sides and edges.

quiz.question: When should the food be shaped in the mat?
choices: Only after it is cold and stiff.
After slicing it into finished portions.
quiz.because: Warm soft food can take the mat’s shape without the cracking caused by stiffness.

quiz.question: What should the block do when cut?
choices: Hold together with an even outline.
quiz.because: A firm coherent block shows that it has taken and retained its shape.

quiz.question: An end of the block became thinner than the rest. What would you change next time?
choices: Press evenly along the whole mat with both hands.
Press only at the centre of the mat.
quiz.because: Distributed pressure prevents local compression from narrowing parts of the block.

comes_after.why: The mat shapes an egg block that has already been cooked in layers.

variant_of.differs: The food is rolled and pressed in a bamboo mat, which gives straight, square edges that hand shaping cannot.
